Runway Gen4.5 · Batch 01 · 21 Aug 2026

Star Mat
Dailies

Six AI-generated hook clips for Reels 1, 3 and 6. Every one is problem-side b-roll only — cones, ladders, bare floor. The mat itself never appears, so the product always stays on-model and cuts to your real footage.

  • 1 use as is
  • 3 use with a fix
  • 2 reject
  • 4 delivered at 1080×1920

Why these are framed, not full-bleed

Runway outputs 1280×720 landscape. Cropping that to a full-bleed vertical Reel means a 2.6× upscale — visibly mushy sitting next to your real camera footage.

So the delivered files place a crisp 1080-wide clip high on a #0D0D0D field with caption room beneath. That is a downscale, so it stays sharp, and it holds your “brand is always dark” rule. Cut from these into your real star-mat-* footage and the AI b-roll reads as a stylistic choice rather than a budget one.

The batch

Use as is 01

Cone Skid

Reel 3 — hook, 0–3s · Day 3

Exactly the shot. A cone gets clipped by a passing shoe, tumbles, and wobbles to a stop on hardwood. The motion is physically believable end to end and the floor reflection sells the room as real.

DirectionNo notes. Cut it straight in under the line “cones move, your data doesn’t.”

1280×720 · 5.0s · 24fps

Use — one fix 02

Ladder Feet

Reel 6 — hook, 0–3s · Day 8

Clean head-on cadence footage. Orange ladder on a gym floor, feet moving in a tight straight line — which is the whole point of the contrarian argument.

DirectionThere is a visible Nike swoosh on the socks and shoes. That is a third-party trademark sitting inside a commercial ad. Blur it or crop tighter before this posts.

1280×720 · 5.0s · 24fps

Use — graphics carry it 03

Plant Foot

Reel 1 — hook, 0–3s · Day 1

Beautiful macro on hardwood with real depth of field and dust in the light. But Runway did not render the ankle rolling outward — what you get is a neutral, technically fine foot plant.

DirectionUsable as the visual bed only. Your red-circle overlay and the voiceover have to do the work of proving the flaw.

1280×720 · 5.0s · 24fps

Use first 2.2s 04

Cone Drift

Reel 3 — b-roll · Day 3

Overhead of five cones at sloppy, uneven spacing — good support for the spacing-drift argument.

DirectionPast roughly 2 seconds the geometry breaks: a cone flattens into a square and scale goes wrong. Already trimmed before that point in the delivered file.

1280×720 · trimmed to 2.2s

Reject 05

Hardwood Brake

Reel 1 — intended b-roll · —

The athlete is running, not decelerating. Knees stay tall, no braking angle, no skid. It is the wrong mechanic for a reel whose entire argument is about stopping.

DirectionRe-prompt with explicit braking language, or keep it as a generic empty-gym establishing shot.

1280×720 · 5.0s · 24fps

Reject 06

Game Cut

Reel 6 — intended payoff · —

The most obviously synthetic clip of the six. The dust plume is desert-scale rather than gym-scale, and the athlete's proportions read as generated on a second look.

DirectionDo not post. Your real footage in star-mat-lateral-skaters.mov covers this beat better.

1280×720 · 5.0s · 24fps

Before any of this posts

  1. Kill the swoosh on Ladder Feet. A third-party trademark inside a commercial ad is the one hard problem in this batch. Blur or crop.
  2. Never let AI b-roll touch the product. These four are safe because the mat is absent. The moment Runway renders a training mat, the geometry, the five-point layout and the 75×75 proportion all come out wrong — and off-model product footage is worse than none.
  3. Pair every AI clip with real footage in the same reel. The AI shot is the problem; your camera is the fix. That contrast is the argument.
  4. Next best fit for Runway is Reel 10 — the frustration montage. Tape peeling off a floor, cones under a car, chalk rubbed half out. All problem-side, no product, no people.
